title: SRE weekly ops sync — prep notes (2026-03-28)
content:
Meeting: SRE weekly ops sync — prep notes
Date: 2026-03-28 (sync 09:30 PT)
Owner / note-taker: Samira Patel
Goal: Quick reliability review before weekly sync; highlight SLO surface, paging trends, top incidents, and action items to triage before broader meeting.

Agenda draft:
- Quick SLO snapshot (2m)
- Paging & alerting trends (5m)
- Top incidents / postmortem status (8m)
- Ongoing mitigations & rollouts (6m)
- Capacity / autoscaling concerns (4m)
- Action items & owners (5m)

SLO snapshot (high-level):
- Inference availability (hosted API): SLO = 99.95% monthly. Current monthly rolling: 99.92% → ~0.03% burn to date. Error budget remaining ~40–45% (estimate).
- P99 generation latency SLO = 300ms (95% of requests under threshold for p50/p95/p99 targets split). Current p99 (30d rolling) = ~360ms (spike last 7 days).
- Embeddings throughput SLO: target 1k req/s sustained for standard tier; currently meeting baseline but tail latency increased during batch window.
- Key note: latency regressions are primary contributor to SLO pressure this period.

Paging / alerting trends (last 14 days):
- Total pages/day (avg): up ~30% vs prior 14-day window.
- Alerts driving pages: model OOMs (22%), kernel selection fallback loops (18%), autoscaler thrash (15%), network blips on eu-west1 (10%).
- New noisy alert: "inference-runtime:kv-cache-miss-rate-high" firing during canary runs of model-v1.4.5.
- Observation: many pages originate from dedicated clusters where v1.4.5 was rolled without kernel compatibility checks.

Top incidents to highlight (brief):
1) INC-2026-03-24-01 — Model OOM cascade on dedicated-pool-3
   - Summary: rollout of quantized model v1.4.5 caused unexpected memory allocation patterns on A100 nodes, leading to OOMs and restarts across replicas.
   - Impact: ~12 minutes degraded availability for customers on Dedicated region-us-west2; elevated p99 latency during failovers.
   - Status: postmortem started, owner Jordan Lee, draft due 2026-04-01.
   - Mitigation taken: rolled back v1.4.5 on affected pools, increased eviction thresholds; temporary increased reserved memory for runtime.

2) INC-2026-03-26-02 — Cache invalidation bug → elevated latency for embeddings route
   - Summary: cache key rotation PR missed a migration step causing repeated cache misses under load and increased backend work.
   - Impact: sustained p95/p99 latency bump for embeddings between 03/26 02:10–03:45 UTC.
   - Status: fix merged (runtime PR #981), deploying canary today. Owner Ethan Chen.
   - Follow-ups: add migration guard in deploy pipeline and a health-check that detects mass cache misses.

3) INC-2026-03-27-03 — Cross-region routing misconfiguration triggers failover storms
   - Summary: a routing policy change for latency-based routing caused simultaneous region failovers during a network blip; autoscaler reacted by overscaling then thrashing.
   - Impact: transient higher cost and additional pages; no customer data loss.
   - Status: mitigation done (reverted routing policy); monitoring OK. Owner Alex Martin.

Observations / hypotheses:
- Common thread: recent rollout activity (v1.4.5) + insufficient kernel/platform compatibility testing on Dedicated pools.
- Autoscaler policy needs smoothing — min replicas too low for steady-state and scale-up delay too long for some tail workloads.
- Runbooks are incomplete for model-specific OOMs (need more explicit steps for rollback & memory tweaks).

Immediate actions (owners & timelines):
- Jordan Lee: continue postmortem for INC-2026-03-24-01; include memory profiles and repro steps; due 2026-04-01.
- Ethan Chen: validate runtime PR #981 canary results; if green, promote and monitor cache-miss metric for 48h; due asap (today).
- Alex Martin: add circuit-breaker for region failover policy and adjust autoscaler cooldown to 5m; planned change 2026-03-30.
- Samira Patel (me): collate SLO dashboard updates and add an "alert noise" dashboard to track pages per alert source; target 2026-03-31.
- On-call rotation lead (Jordan/Ethan): add a temporary preflight checklist for model rollouts on Dedicated (kernel compatibility matrix, memory smoke test, canary traffic profile).

Longer-term / backlog items:
- Improve kernel-selection testing matrix and add automated compatibility tests for new quantized models. (Research/Applied-ML + Serving Runtime)
- Revisit batching and prefix cache heuristics to reduce backend CPU spikes during cache misses. (Serving runtime)
- Add SLO-driven deploy gating: block model rollout if estimated error budget impact > 5% for the month. (Platform)

Runbooks / links to review in meeting:
- SLO dashboards: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SRE/SLO+dashboards
- INC-2026-03-24-01 (postmortem draft) — CORE-842
- Runtime PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/981
- PagerDuty incident list: https://redwood.pagerduty.com/incidents

Prep checklist for sync:
- Pull last 14d paging trends (Jordan)
- Confirm canary deploy status for PR #981 (Ethan)
- Snapshot of SLOs and error budget (Samira)
- Update on autoscaler policy change (Alex)

Notes / talking points for meeting:
- Emphasize that most pages are correlated with recent rollouts — we should harden rollout preflight and add gating.
- Ask Leadership for capacity commit if we need to increase min replicas across Dedicated for steady-state reliability (estimate cost impact ~= +8–12% infra spend).
- Seek agreement on a temporary freeze of non-critical rollouts to Dedicated until compatibility tests are in place.

Action items (to capture at meeting close):
- [Jordan] Postmortem draft + memory-profile attachment — due 2026-04-01.
- [Ethan] Promote cache fix if canary green; add migration guard to pipeline — due ASAP.
- [Alex] Implement routing circuit-breaker + autoscaler cooldown change — plan by 2026-03-30.
- [Samira] Create alert-noise dashboard and share link in channel — due 2026-03-31.
- [On-call lead] Draft model-rollout preflight checklist and publish to runbooks — due 2026-04-02.

Open questions for sync:
- Do we have budget approval for a temporary min-replica increase on Dedicated?
- Tolerance for rollout freeze across Dedicated vs. targeted freeze only for quantized models?
- Who will own adding the SLO-driven deploy gating (Platform vs. SRE)?

Misc notes / scratchpad:
- Quick metric snippets: last 7d average pages/day = 18 (prev 14d window = 14); median page time-to-resolve = 9m; avg escalations/day = 1.2.
- Consider tagging noisy alerts in PD so we can suppress low-actionability ones during working hours.

---
This is a working prep doc — will tidy after internal review. Add anything else you want on thread and I will fold into the meeting agenda.
